message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for a man to expect his boss to be upset because he submitted a report by the deadline. Hmm, let me break this down. First, I need to understand the scenario. The person submitted a report exactly on the deadline. Now, he's expecting his boss to be upset. Is that justified? Well, in most workplaces, meeting deadlines is a good thing. It shows responsibility and time management. So, if the report was submitted on time, why would the boss be upset? Maybe the person is worried about the quality of the report. If the report was rushed or had errors, that could be a problem. But if it's thorough and meets all the requirements, then the boss should be satisfied. Another angle is the company culture. Some companies might prefer reports to be submitted early rather than on the deadline. Maybe the boss expects things to be done a bit ahead of time. But that's not always the case. Most places are okay with on-time submissions. Also, maybe the person has a history of missing deadlines, so this time, even though he met it, the boss is still concerned. But if he's consistently meeting deadlines now, that should be a positive sign. I'm also thinking about communication. If the person communicated with the boss about the progress and confirmed the deadline, that would set clear expectations. Without that, the boss might have assumptions that the report would be done earlier. So, putting it all together, unless there's something else wrong with the report, expecting the boss to be upset for submitting on time doesn't seem justified. It might even come off as insecure or lacking confidence in his work. Therefore, I think it's not right to expect the boss to be upset just for meeting the deadline. It's more appropriate to expect positive feedback or at least neutral acceptance.
